answer: I'd like to talk about a promise I made to my younger sister, who means a great deal to me. A promise I made and worked hard to keep was when I assured her I would help her prepare for her exams. It was about a year ago, before her HSC exams, and she was struggling with accounting, which happens to be one of my stronger subjects from my BBA. At the time I was extremely busy at work, so it was a fairly bold commitment. She was quite anxious and had started to lose confidence, which worried all of us. As the weeks went on, keeping that promise became genuinely [[demanding]], because my own workload kept [[piling up]]. There were evenings when I was exhausted and tempted to cancel, but I felt a strong sense of [[obligation]] not to let her down. So I pushed through, spending several evenings a week going over her subjects with her at the dining table after dinner. I also made her a simple timetable so she could see her progress week by week. My mother kept us going with endless cups of tea. When she eventually did well, the pride I felt was [[immense]], and our bond grew even stronger. Keeping that promise meant missing a few cricket matches with friends, but I never regretted it for a moment. What I learned was that keeping a promise, especially an inconvenient one, is a real measure of [[character]]. Honestly, seeing how much my help meant to her made every tiring evening worthwhile. It reinforced my belief that your word should always mean something.

followUps.q: Do you think it is important to keep promises?
followUps.answer: Absolutely. If you break promises often, people stop trusting you, and that trust is very hard to win back. So I try not to promise anything unless I am sure I can deliver.

followUps.q: Does your sister still ask you for help with her studies?
followUps.answer: Sometimes, but less and less. She is at university now and very hard-working, so these days she is more likely to correct my mistakes than ask me to explain anything.

note: Specified HSC accounting help at home after dinner; plain-ish 'challenging' replaced by 'demanding'; added 'piling up'.
